meta.description: If a parent, grandparent or great-grandparent fled or was persecuted in Germany or Austria, you may qualify for citizenship. Free 2-minute eligibility check and a call with a lawyer.
meta.serviceName: German and Austrian citizenship by descent
meta.offerDescription: Free eligibility check and consultation call

hero.title: Your family history could open the door to European citizenship.
hero.lead: If a parent, grandparent or great-grandparent fled or was persecuted in Germany or Austria, provisions in German and Austrian law may allow you, and your children, to seek citizenship today.
hero.note: This applies particularly to descendants of Jewish families who were forced to leave Germany or Austria during the Nazi era.

why.kicker: Why this may apply to you
why.title: Most families never knew this history still counted.
why.photoAlt: Hands holding a historical family photograph beside old letters and a map of Central Europe
story: “Our family rarely spoke about what happened.”
“I never realized that history could still create rights today.”
why.p1: Germany and Austria both created ways for descendants of people persecuted or driven out during the Nazi era to reclaim the citizenship their family lost. The provisions have widened in recent years, so families told long ago that they did not qualify often do now.
why.p2: You do not need documents, German, or a complete family tree to begin. Only a rough sense of who left, and when.

routes.title: Your family's country decides the route. We work out which.

items.title: Restoration under German law
items.body: For descendants of those who lost or were denied German citizenship between 1933 and 1945. The provisions have widened in recent years.

items.title: Citizenship for descendants
items.body: For descendants of those who fled Austria because of persecution, with no limit on how many generations back the line reaches.

people.name: Anat Levi
people.bio: Anat Levi is the managing partner of Decker Pex Levi and oversees the firm's citizenship practice. She specialises in German and Austrian citizenship by descent, working through the family history and the records each route requires. Clients describe her as professional and efficient, and write about the personal attention that left them feeling their case was in good hands.

people.name: Michael Decker
people.bio: Michael Decker is a founding partner of the firm. He was among the first lawyers in Israel to develop this field, obtaining German and Austrian passports for descendants under the updated citizenship laws. He brings decades of experience in immigration and citizenship law across Israel and Europe.

people.name: Yehoshua Pex
people.bio: Yehoshua Pex is a founding partner of the firm and its link to clients around the world. The practice serves families in Hebrew, English, Russian, Ukrainian, Arabic, German, Dutch and Spanish, so people can discuss their family history in their own language. Client reviews single him out as reliable, professional, and providing service at the highest level.

reviews.name: Jason Miller
reviews.text: DP Lower made a complicated process surprisingly simple. They were responsive, organized, and clear about what documents I needed at every stage. I'm very happy with the service and would absolutely recommend their team.

reviews.name: Sarah Klein
reviews.text: I contacted DP Lower because my grandmother was born in Germany and I had no idea whether that could make me eligible for citizenship. They explained everything clearly and helped me understand the process from the very beginning. Excellent experience.

reviews.name: David Bernstein
reviews.text: Professional from start to finish. The team helped me locate the documents I needed and kept me updated throughout the process. Getting my German citizenship was something I had been thinking about for years, and I'm glad I finally did it with them.

reviews.name: Emily Goldberg
reviews.text: What I appreciated most was how patient everyone was. I had a lot of questions about my family history and eligibility, and I never felt rushed. They walked me through each step and made the whole experience much less intimidating.

reviews.name: Jonathan Weiss
reviews.text: Great team and very professional service. They knew exactly what was required for my Austrian citizenship case and guided me through the documentation step by step. Highly recommended.

reviews.name: Rachel Hoffman
reviews.text: My family had very limited information about my grandfather's life in Germany, so I assumed the process would be almost impossible. DP Lower helped us understand what was missing and how to move forward. Their guidance made a huge difference.

reviews.name: Daniel Friedman
reviews.text: From the initial eligibility check through the documentation process, everything was clear and well organized. I always knew what stage my application was at and what was needed from me next. Very positive experience.

reviews.name: Jessica Stein
reviews.text: I started looking into German citizenship mainly because I wanted my children to have more opportunities to live and study in Europe in the future. DP Lower made the process easy to understand and supported our family throughout. I'm incredibly grateful.

reviews.name: Robert Adler
reviews.text: Excellent communication and very knowledgeable people. Whenever I had a question, someone was there to explain what was happening. The process took time, but I always felt that my case was being handled professionally.

reviews.name: Lauren Kaplan
reviews.text: I honestly expected the citizenship process to be overwhelming. It wasn't. The team broke everything down into manageable steps, helped with the documents, and kept things moving. A very professional and reassuring experience.

reviews.name: Andrew Feldman
reviews.text: My grandfather left Austria many years ago, and I wasn't even sure our family would qualify. DP Lower reviewed our situation, explained the process clearly, and guided us through everything that followed. I would definitely recommend speaking with them if you have Austrian family history.

reviews.name: Barbara Levine
reviews.text: I began this process because I wanted my grandchildren to have the opportunity to study and build a future in Europe if they choose to. DP Lower was patient, kind, and extremely professional throughout the entire process. For our family, obtaining European citizenship means giving the next generation more possibilities.

benefits.title: One decision today can open Europe for the next generation.
benefits.lead: An EU passport isn't a document you use once. It stays in the family, and it passes on.

items.title: Live in Europe
items.body: As an EU citizen you may live in EU member states, subject to each state's rules.

items.title: Work
items.body: Access to employment across the EU without a separate work permit.

items.title: Study
items.body: European universities at domestic rather than international rates.

items.title: Travel
items.body: An EU passport alongside the one you already hold.

items.title: Your children
items.body: Citizenship may pass to the next generation, subject to applicable rules.

benefits.disclaimer: Rights associated with EU citizenship are subject to the rules of each member state. Nothing here is a guarantee of eligibility or of citizenship being granted.
